question: Does a soft temporal re-ranking term behave consistently across different retriever families (BM25 and several dense encoders) and top-k budgets, or is any gain specific to one retriever configuration?
description: The idea claims retrieval-agnosticism, but TempRALM instantiates a single retriever (Atlas/Contriever) and no retrieved work evaluates a temporal re-ranking wrapper across multiple sparse and dense retrievers under matched budgets. It is unknown whether the soft temporal term's effect is stable across retrievers or is an artifact of one embedding space, chunking scheme and top-k.
rationale: Retrieval-agnosticism is a headline claim of the idea; without cross-retriever evidence under matched budgets the claim is unsupported even if one configuration improves.
